html:
The Koreguaje, who call themselves Korebaju, are an Indigenous people of the Caquetá department in the Colombian Amazon, living mostly along the Orteguaza River and its tributaries. Their language belongs to the western branch of the Tucanoan family, a cousin of the Eastern Tucanoan languages spoken by the Siriano and others.

They fished, hunted and grew manioc and plantains in forest gardens. Capuchin missions and settlers moving down from the Andes in the 1900s took much of their land. Today a few thousand live in reserves in Colombia.
